title: Grill round 2: follow-ups on base precedence, the Base line and multiple PRs per repository
summary:
Thanks, round 1 is complete. Three of your answers raise follow-ups the plan can't settle by itself:

- **Q2 (base precedence):** you put the stored base first. Against the real app-repo case, that picks a stale base.
- **Q13 (Base line):** you want a `Base:` line *and* the link. That needs a rule for when they disagree.
- **Q14 (multiple PRs per repository):** now in scope. It raises a trust question, a data question and a few edges.

The last section is defaults derived from your answers. Confirm or override.
proven: Accepted as you answered: create-time base stored (migration 092), HEAD records the checked-out branch only if it's on the remote, a missing base fails that repo clearly, attribution by link or label with the blind fallback dropped, newest matching proposal per repository across runs, root-task title as the no-proposal fallback (flagged), an editable confirm list, the single Create PR chip prefills the base, per-forge destination links, the prompt names the known base with an escape clause, and you'll update your own pipeline step text.

proven.text: **How PRs are stamped today.** One URL per repository entry (`repositories[].prUrl`), or `tasks.pr_url` for a single-repo task. First write wins, and Create all PRs skips any entry that already has one.

questions.title: The stored base is first. What happens when the agent moved the branch onto another base?
questions.why: Your Q2 order (stored base → agent's base → default) would have opened the real **app** PR against the stale feature branch. It also makes the escape clause you chose for the prompt (Q12: "unless you moved the branch onto another base") have no effect on Create all PRs.
questions.context:
Your round-1 answer to Q2: **1. stored base, 2. agent's link, 3. remote default.**

In the real run, the agent reset the app repo's task branch onto `origin/main`. The stored base (a feature branch) is no longer an ancestor of the head (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` fails). The agent's reply said the PR should target `main`.

The editable confirm list (Q9) will show the base either way. The question is what it **preselects**.

options.label: Stored base first, unless git proves it stale; then the agent's base
options.description: "Stale" means the stored base's remote tip isn't an ancestor of the head. The confirm list shows both when they differ.
options.consequence: Gets both real repos right with no manual edit. One extra `git merge-base` per repository.

options.label: Stored base always first; the confirm list flags a different agent base
options.description: e.g. "agent suggests `main`", and you change it by hand.
options.consequence: Simple and predictable. The real app PR needs a manual base change every time.

options.label: Switch to the agent's base first (my round-1 recommendation)
options.consequence: The agent can override a correct stored base with a wrong one. The confirm list is the safety net.

recommendation.reason: It keeps your stored-first order, and still gets the real app repo right without trusting the agent when git agrees with the stored base.

questions.title: The agent's `Base:` line and its link name different branches. Which is "the agent's base"?
questions.why: You chose both a `Base:` line and a destination link (Q13). They can disagree, for example an agent that writes `Base: develop` but pastes git's `pull/new/` link.
questions.context: Your round-1 answer to Q13: **"Yes, plus the link."**

options.label: The `Base:` line wins; the confirm list flags the mismatch
options.consequence: The explicit statement beats a URL the agent may have copied from git's output.

options.label: The link wins; flag the mismatch
options.consequence: The link is what the user would actually click.

options.label: Ignore both (no agent base) and flag it
options.consequence: Falls to the next source. Safest, but it wastes a usable signal.

recommendation.reason: A link is often pasted from git's push output (default-branch link) even when the agent knows the right base. The line is the deliberate statement.

sections.title: More than one PR per repository (now in scope)
sections.intro: You moved Q14 in scope: one PR per matching proposal. Today a repository's only PR head is its live checkout. A second proposal names **another branch**, and that changes who decides what gets opened.

questions.title: Which branches may Create all PRs open a PR *from*, besides each repository's live checkout?
questions.why: The head would come from agent-written text. A confused or prompt-injected agent could name any branch on that remote, a teammate's included, and agetor would open a public PR for it under your forge token.
questions.context: The real reply proposed a second branch in the app repo. The link already proves it's on that repository's remote. It does *not* prove the branch belongs to this task.

options.label: Any branch on that repository's remote that a proposal names; shown in the confirm list **unchecked** by default
options.consequence: Every extra PR takes your explicit tick. The live-head PR stays checked.

options.label: Same, but **checked** by default
options.consequence: One click opens them all. A stray branch name becomes a public PR unless you notice and untick it.

options.label: Only branches that contain commits made during this task (an author/time check against the task's runs)
options.consequence: Tighter, but a heuristic with its own edge cases (rebased or squashed commits). More code and tests.

recommendation.reason: You get every proposed PR, and the one decision agent text can't make on its own (opening a PR from a branch it named) stays yours.

questions.title: How are the extra PRs recorded on the task?
questions.why: Recording them changes the task's data shape, which the run panel, task card, context menu, pipelines and the API all read. Not recording them means a second press opens duplicates.
questions.context: `prUrl` is read today by about 15 webview, core and shared modules (the PR link, the button gate, the context menu, pipeline copy, repo removal). Repository entries live in JSON, so a new field there needs no column. A single-repo task's PRs live in `tasks.pr_url`.

options.label: Keep `prUrl` as the live-head PR. Add a list of extra PRs (`{head, base, url}`) per repository entry, and for a single-repo task in migration 092
options.consequence: Existing readers don't change. The run panel lists the extra PRs. Duplicates are skipped by head.

options.label: Replace `prUrl` with a list everywhere
options.consequence: Cleaner model, but every `prUrl` reader and the API shape change, and the CLI and TUI follow.

options.label: Don't record them; report their links in the toast only
options.consequence: No data change. A second press opens them again, unless the forge's "PR already exists" answer is turned into a skip.

recommendation.reason: Every existing reader keeps working and duplicates are still prevented. Same migration, one more field.

questions.title: A **single-repository** task whose reply proposes two PRs: does it get this too?
questions.why: Single-repo tasks have no Create all PRs button, only the one Create PR chip, which opens the composer for the live-head proposal.

options.label: No: multi-repo Create all PRs only. The single chip keeps one PR (the live-head proposal)
options.consequence: The second PR on a single-repo task stays manual, through the link in the reply.

options.label: Yes: when the reply has more than one proposal, the single chip lets you pick which one to open in the composer
options.consequence: A small picker on the chip, plus the extra-PR stamping for single-repo tasks.

options.label: Yes: show Create all PRs (with the same confirm list) on single-repo tasks with more than one proposal
options.consequence: The same flow everywhere. Larger UI change on the single-repo panel.

recommendation.reason: The bug and the button are multi-repo. A single-repo multi-PR flow is a new surface, so it's a different ticket unless you want it now.

sections.title: Confirm or override (derived from your answers)

recommendation.value: The stored create-time base belongs to the task branch only. An extra PR's base is the agent's base (`Base:` line, then link), then the remote default. It's editable in the confirm list.
recommendation.reason: The task's stored base says nothing about another branch.

questions.title: An extra head that isn't on the remote

recommendation.value: Shown disabled in the confirm list: "branch `<x>` isn't on origin". No PR is attempted.
recommendation.reason: Same rule as a missing base: fail clearly, never guess.

recommendation.value: The newest matching proposal per (repository, head) across runs, extending your round-1 Q7 answer from per-repository.
recommendation.reason: With several PRs per repository, the head is what tells two proposals apart.

recommendation.value: A head already stamped (live or extra) is skipped. A forge "a pull request already exists" answer is shown as "already open" (with the URL when the forge returns one), not as a failure.
recommendation.reason: Makes a second press safe, as today.

recommendation.value: Both prompts (single and multi) ask for a `Base: <branch>` line right above the link, inside each repository's block for multi.
recommendation.reason: The parser then finds the line, the link, the title and the description in a fixed order.
